absent: Early portion of share transfer setup before fragment validation, including handle creation and total length determination.
Semantics of transmit mapping, unmapping, lend versus share transfer, reclaim, and fragment transmit handlers referenced by dispatch.
Layout and version differences of endpoint access and constituent structures beyond offset and count uses.
Host unshare implementation and conditions that could trigger its warning.
Firmware reclaim flag handling and full error translation beyond observed branches.
Mailbox page count and page size values and descriptor buffer capacity computation.
Pass-through forwarding path for supported but unhandled calls and nonstandard call policy enforcement.
Hypervisor spinlock implementation and ordering guarantees beyond acquire and release uses.
Build integration and runtime consumption of the emitted relocation container and per-section symbols.

findings.text: Host FF-A request gate callable with a host CPU context and a function identifier. It declines non FF-A identifiers, rejects every identifier except version negotiation before negotiation completes, dispatches a fixed set of memory and partition operations to dedicated handlers, passes through recognized but unclaimed identifiers, and otherwise reports unsupported while installing a result into the host context.

Early hypervisor FF-A capability probe and buffer carve-out. It stays inactive when the platform management interface is too old or when firmware declines versioning, otherwise clamps the negotiated minor version to an upper bound, partitions a caller supplied page span into transmit plus receive plus descriptor areas, and initializes buffer and version synchronization objects.

Host build tool entry that expects exactly one ELF object path argument, validates and maps that object, opens a data plus relocation container, walks relocation sections to produce hypervisor relocation entries, closes the container, and reports usage failure or success through process exit status.

Process-global ELF view holding an input path for diagnostics, a mapped image base, an image size, plus derived pointers to the ELF header and section header table and section name storage. Helpers resolve typed pointers by file offset, resolve section headers by index or offset, and derive names and contents with endian-correct conversions.

Mutual exclusion around hypervisor FF-A version state. Version query handling acquires it while inspecting and possibly updating the negotiated version and completion flag, then releases it on every outcome path.

Mutual exclusion around host side mailbox access during share completion and partition query. Holders verify receive buffer presence, bound lengths against mailbox capacity, copy between hypervisor and host or descriptor storage, interact with firmware, and release before returning a translated status.

Version state starts unnegotiated with a firmware maximum. A major mismatch is declined. Once negotiated, requests below the stored minor are declined while others confirm the stored value. Before completion a downgrade attempt is first offered to firmware and adopted only on firmware acceptance, then a post probe must succeed before the completion flag is published with release ordering.

Dispatch begins with a non FF-A bypass, then a pre-negotiation gate that allows only versioning. Negotiated calls reach dedicated handlers for features, mapping, share, lend, reclaim, fragment continuation, version and partition query. Unhandled identifiers either pass through when marked supported or complete locally as unsupported.

Share completion validates an initial fragment length and constituent location against total length and mailbox capacity, stages bytes into a descriptor area, repeatedly requests further fragments by handle and offset while each reply indicates continuation, validates the final constituent table location, then issues reclaim and on reclaim success releases the described ranges with a warning on unexpected failure.

Support test denies memory retrieve and relinquish and pause and resume and fragment receive and donate operations, denies indirect message send poll and wait operations, denies narrow aliases of wide operations, denies notification management operations, and denies a set of optional newer interfaces for direct messaging extensions and console and register-based partition discovery, while allowing all other function identifiers.

Feature query first applies the support test and reports unsupported when denied. Share and lend queries in either width succeed with a property value indicating no dynamic buffer capability. All other supported queries are left unhandled so the caller can pass them through.

Post-negotiation probe requires a successful identifier query returning the expected host identifier, requires successful feature interrogation for wide mapping, accepts only three documented minimum buffer size encodings, translates them to corresponding byte sizes, and fails when the minimum exceeds a single page or when any encoding or status check is unexpected.

Partition discovery requires an established host receive area, forwards caller supplied identity and flags to firmware, stops on firmware failure or empty count, honors a count-only flag on newer versions, derives per-entry size from firmware on newer versions and from a fixed legacy size on the initial version, bounds total copy against mailbox capacity, and stages firmware entries into host storage under lock.

Initialization probes firmware with a maximum minor version, remains dormant on firmware refusal or major mismatch, otherwise retains the lesser of firmware and local maxima, then subdivides caller pages into fixed-count transmit and receive mailboxes with the remainder as descriptor space and creates unlocked buffer state plus version lock.

Loader records the path, opens and sizes the file, maps it read-only, checks minimum header size and four magic bytes, enforces 64-bit class with expected endianness and relocatable type for the AArch64 machine, then locates the section table and section name storage while rejecting zero offsets and undefined section indices.

Relocation emission visits only relocation-with-addend sections, aborts on old-style relocation sections, ignores sections whose names lack the hypervisor prefix, verifies each entry offset lies inside its origin section, emits an entry only for absolute 64-bit data references, silently permits absolute 32-bit and position-relative and program-counter-relative and control-flow and move-wide group references, and aborts on any other relocation number.

Diagnostic helpers report the input path with a formatted message or system error and terminate the process, while assertion helpers capture both operands once and abort with operand values and line number when the requested equality or inequality or ordering comparison does not hold.
Prefix test compares only the length of the candidate prefix, and name and content helpers derive section strings and bytes from the section table using endian-correct name offsets and file offsets.

Hypervisor section naming facts: the section prefix is a dot followed by three lower case letters h y p, the relocation container extends that prefix with dot r e l o c, and the per-section symbol prefix is two underscores plus h y p plus underscore plus s e c t i o n plus underscore.

Endian conversion facts: one build variant interprets 16 plus 32 plus 64 bit ELF fields as little endian with matching ELF data encoding, while the alternate variant interprets the same widths as big endian with the corresponding alternate encoding.

Numeric relocation facts for data and relative group: R_AARCH64_ABS64 equals 257 with R_AARCH64_ABS32 equals 258 with R_AARCH64_PREL64 equals 260 with R_AARCH64_PREL32 equals 261 with R_AARCH64_PREL16 equals 262 with R_AARCH64_PLT32 equals 314.

Numeric relocation facts for program counter relative addressing: R_AARCH64_LD_PREL_LO19 equals 273 with R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_LO21 equals 274 with R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21 equals 275 with R_AARCH64_ADR_PREL_PG_HI21_NC equals 276 with R_AARCH64_ADD_ABS_LO12_NC equals 277 with R_AARCH64_LDST8_ABS_LO12_NC equals 278 with R_AARCH64_LDST16_ABS_LO12_NC equals 284 with R_AARCH64_LDST32_ABS_LO12_NC equals 285 with R_AARCH64_LDST64_ABS_LO12_NC equals 286 with R_AARCH64_LDST128_ABS_LO12_NC equals 299.

Numeric relocation facts for branches and move wide group: R_AARCH64_TSTBR14 equals 279 with R_AARCH64_CONDBR19 equals 280 with R_AARCH64_JUMP26 equals 282 with R_AARCH64_CALL26 equals 283 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G0 equals 287 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G0_NC equals 288 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G1 equals 289 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G1_NC equals 290 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G2 equals 291 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G2_NC equals 292 with R_AARCH64_MOVW_PREL_G3 equals 293.

Share completion hazards include trusting firmware supplied offsets only after explicit bounds checks, releasing the receive channel on every early validation failure, translating distinct failures into invalid parameters versus aborted versus no memory, and treating reclaim failure as terminal without unsharing while treating post-reclaim unshare failure as a warning condition.

Partition and version hazards include reporting busy when host receive storage is absent, aborting when firmware entry count would overflow mailbox capacity, serializing concurrent version queries to avoid downgrade races, and blocking all non-version calls until release-acquire publication of negotiation success.

Tool hazards include immediate termination on unexpected relocation or section kinds, on out-of-range relocation offsets, on missing or malformed ELF structure, and on incorrect invocation arity, plus a monotonically increasing relocation slot index that assumes single-threaded emission.
